category.name: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws

rule.name: Untrusted Inputs: $_REQUEST, $_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE
rule.rule_desc: The code reads request, query, form or cookie input through a PHP superglobal. Reading input alone does not establish an unsafe use or a vulnerability.
rule.vuln_desc: If caller-controlled values reach a sensitive operation without suitable constraints, they may alter queries, filesystem paths, output or application state. The actual data flow and trust boundary must be established.
rule.developer: Validate input against the operation's intended type and policy, bind query values, encode output for its destination and enforce authorization at sensitive operations.
rule.reviewer: Trace superglobal input flow to sensitive sinks and verify validation and sanitization coverage. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Command Injection: shell_exec, exec, passthru, system, popen, backtick
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
rule.vuln_desc: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
rule.developer: Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.
rule.reviewer: Inspect shell_exec, exec, passthru, system, popen, and backtick usage for untrusted input flow and control enforcement. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.developer: Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.
rule.reviewer: Trace input flow into eval, exec, or assert sinks and verify that strict constraints prevent attacker-controlled execution. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Object Injection via Serialization
rule.rule_desc: The application calls object-capable PHP deserialization. Identify the input trust and effective allowed_classes policy at this specific call; serialization alone and unrelated JSON decoding do not establish or mitigate object injection.
rule.vuln_desc: A crafted untrusted payload may instantiate dangerous types or trigger object behavior that executes code, modifies state, or exhausts resources when the parser permits those operations.
rule.developer: Use a data-only format and a safe loader for untrusted input. Disable automatic object or type construction, allowlist required types, and bound parsing size and complexity.
rule.reviewer: Trace whether untrusted input reaches unserialize or related deserialization paths and verify that class restrictions and payload trust checks are enforced. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via PHP_SELF
rule.rule_desc: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
rule.developer: Use automatic context-aware output encoding and data-only DOM APIs. Sanitize deliberately accepted rich HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and avoid marking untrusted content as safe.
rule.reviewer: Check reflected output contexts for proper encoding and safe rendering behavior. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure Redirect: header() with Location
rule.rule_desc: The code handles a link, redirect, or externally selected navigation target. Validate the effective destination and any action triggered by the receiving handler.
rule.vuln_desc: A crafted destination or link may direct users to a phishing site, leak URL-carried secrets, or trigger unauthorized operations if routing trusts external parameters without the required access checks.
rule.developer: Allowlist schemes, hosts, paths, and operations. Validate parsed link parameters, avoid credentials in URLs, and require authentication and authorization before sensitive actions.
rule.reviewer: Inspect Location header construction and validation controls for open redirect risk. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure File Inclusion: include(), require()
rule.rule_desc: The code accesses, creates, deletes, or shares filesystem data. Resolve path provenance, destination containment, permission modes, and any concurrent access.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.
rule.developer: Resolve paths beneath a fixed permitted root and verify containment and effective permissions. Use safe exclusive temporary-file creation, restrict sharing, and account for symlinks and concurrent changes.
rule.reviewer: Trace input usage in include and require path construction and verify canonical validation and allowlisting controls. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure Variable Injection: extract()
rule.rule_desc: Externally supplied array keys may be converted into local variable names.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker may overwrite security-relevant variables or alter program decisions when imported keys collide with trusted local state.
rule.developer: Avoid importing untrusted keys into the local namespace. Parse into a dedicated data structure and explicitly assign only expected fields.
rule.reviewer: Examine extract usage with request-derived arrays and variable scope impact. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.reviewer: Inspect response and error handling paths for exposure of stack traces or internal details. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Deprecated and Potentially Insecure SQL Functions
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
rule.vuln_desc: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.
rule.reviewer: Inspect deprecated SQL API usage and query construction patterns for untrusted input influence. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Deprecated Regular Expression Functions
rule.rule_desc: The source references a dependency, version, or deprecated API. Resolve the actual deployed version and supported behavior before deciding whether it needs replacement.
rule.vuln_desc: A reachable vulnerability in an unsupported or affected dependency may compromise the application with its privileges. A version declaration or deprecated API alone does not establish that such a vulnerability is present.
rule.developer: Inventory resolved dependencies and runtime versions, compare them with authoritative advisories and support policy, and migrate affected or unsupported components to tested supported replacements.
rule.reviewer: Locate deprecated API usage and validate migration completeness to secure alternatives. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: XXE: DOMDocument loadXML Without Entity Disablement
rule.rule_desc: The code parses or transforms XML. Resolve external entity, DTD, and resource-loading settings for the actual parser instance.
rule.vuln_desc: If external resources or entity expansion are permitted for untrusted XML, an attacker may read local files, make requests to internal services, or exhaust parser resources.
rule.developer: Disable external entities and DTD loading for untrusted XML, use a restrictive resolver, and enforce input-size and expansion limits on the effective parser.
rule.reviewer: Confirm that libxml_disable_entity_loader(true) or equivalent protections are applied before all XML parsing of untrusted data. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
